mechanism: Avoid a store only when attachment contents are provably dead at pass end.
risk: Later resolve, sampling, transfer or readback could depend on discarded contents.
experiment: Replay identical passes; compare output/readback and attachment store counters when available.

mechanism: Compare one explicit multisample resolve against the baseline resolve schedule.
risk: Sample counts, framebuffer compatibility and color encoding can invalidate equivalence.
experiment: Compare framebuffer completeness, pixel goldens and interleaved device timing for one resolve.
fallback: Keep baseline resolve order and path.

mechanism: Compare compute then sampled draw with fragment-only work for the same output.
risk: Incorrect producer-to-consumer barriers or image formats can corrupt results.
experiment: Compare numeric output and time with the required texture-fetch barrier and identical work.
fallback: Retain the existing validated fragment route.

mechanism: Compare coherent EXT framebuffer fetch with an explicit ping-pong pass.
risk: Advertisement does not prove shader support, observed correct draws or stability.
experiment: Check exact shaders and content against ping-pong goldens before any timing run.

mechanism: Test a bounded ring that reuses storage only after its previous consumer retires.
risk: Unsatisfied or cross-context fences can cause corruption; extra slots increase residency.
experiment: Check retirement and timeout controls, then compare frame latency and memory at fixed workload.
fallback: Keep the existing synchronized ownership path.

mechanism: Compare an explicitly complete mip chain and constrained LOD on distant geometry.
risk: Missing mip levels or temporal aliasing can regress image correctness.
experiment: Replay fixed cameras; compare temporal image goldens and measure texture traffic if supported.
fallback: Keep the prior sampler and LOD settings.
